conventions.convention: The horizon T is a finite nonnegative integer. States are indexed 0 through T, observations 1 through T, and trajectory coordinates are interleaved as (X0,X1,Y1,…,XT,YT). At T=0 the trajectory law is the initial law.

State and observation spaces are standard Borel, equipped with finite product sigma-algebras. The displayed product of transition and observation kernels denotes ordered successive integration, without assuming densities, time homogeneity, or stationarity. AC is assumed.

State and observation dimensions are positive integers and may vary with time. Matrices are deterministic, every covariance is symmetric positive semidefinite, and the initial vector and all process and observation noise vectors are mutually independent.
Singular Gaussian covariance matrices are permitted. Positive definiteness is required separately whenever an innovation covariance is inverted.
In the one-step innovation example there are no earlier observations: the predicted mean is E[X1], the state prediction covariance is Var(X1), and the innovation covariance is Var(Y1−H1 E[X1]).

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. For finite T≥0, standard-Borel state and observation spaces, an initial probability measure, and transition and observation probability kernels as specified, there is a unique probability measure on the interleaved finite product whose rectangle probabilities are the ordered iterated kernel integrals. For T=0 this is the initial law.

Assume AC and a finite-horizon model of the linear-Gaussian definition. Mutually independent Gaussian initial and noise vectors with the stated laws exist; their recursions induce the general kernel-product law. For the interleaved path ZT and stacked noises WT, ZT=MT WT for a deterministic matrix MT, and ZT has normal law with mean MT aT and covariance MT ΣT MTᵀ. The covariance may be singular.

Assume AC. A finite nonempty stack of mutually independent Gaussian vectors of positive finite dimensions has multivariate normal law with stacked means and block-diagonal covariance. Each covariance is symmetric positive semidefinite; no covariance block needs to be invertible.

Under AC, a finite-horizon state-space model specifies standard-Borel state and observation spaces, an initial probability measure, transition probability kernels Kt from E(t−1) to Et, and observation probability kernels Gt from Et to Ft. Its law is the unique ordered iterated kernel-product law on the interleaved trajectory space.

Under AC, the finite-horizon linear-Gaussian model has initial law N(m0,P0), transition kernels N(Ft x,Qt), and observation kernels N(Ht x,Rt), with deterministic dimension-compatible matrices and symmetric positive-semidefinite covariances. Its independent-noise representation uses mutually independent Gaussian initial, process, and observation vectors and the stated linear recursions.

published_dependencies.used_for: Explicit choice assumption inherited by Gaussian existence, characteristic-function uniqueness, Cramer–Wold, and Ionescu–Tulcea.
Mutual independence means independence of generated sigma-algebras; scalar projections preserve the needed independence.
Measurability and product joint law of a finite independent stack.
Gaussian existence, projection characterization, means and covariances, including singular covariance matrices.
Gaussian transform formula and uniqueness, used for stacked Gaussian vectors and translated noise kernels.
Transforms of scalar affine maps and finite independent sums.
Identification of scalar normal projection laws from their characteristic functions.
Identification of the stacked vector law from all scalar projection laws.
The measurable-space convention imposed on state and observation spaces.
Trajectory sigma-algebras, measurable coordinate projections, and the singleton empty product.
Standard-Borel structure of finite trajectory spaces, including boundary cases.
Pointwise probability sections and measurable evaluations of lifted and Gaussian kernels.
The initial law and total-mass-one convention.
Existence and uniqueness for history-dependent lifted kernels, with singleton tails reducing the countable construction to a finite horizon.
Measurability of translated Gaussian kernel evaluations using constant probability kernels.
Finite product probability space realizing all independent Gaussian noise vectors.
Iterated nonnegative integration identifying the recursive noise construction with the ordered kernel-product law.
Centered second-moment conventions in both examples.
Zero-variance scalar Gaussian laws are point masses.
Covariance bilinearity and the cross-covariance calculation distinguishing the two joint laws.
Vanishing covariance of independent centered initial and observation noise variables.
Page-level interpretation of the latent trajectory and observed coordinate record as measurable random elements.
Page-level interpretation of the observed record law as a coordinate pushforward.
